title: Three-phase hierarchical model-based and hybrid inference
author: Saarela, Varvia, et al.

steps.title: Set superpopulation statistics
steps.instruction: Record the superpopulation means μY=62.62, μX=10.94, μZ=7.16, μP=8.28; standard deviations sdY=49.53, sdX=6.30, sdZ=4.34, sdP=5.69; correlations rYX=0.77, rXZ=0.75, rZP=0.76; and dataset sizes nI=102, nII=94, nIII=31, nIV=72, N=157,600, 38,400, 2 as listed in Table 5.

steps.title: Compute true model parameters
steps.instruction: Using the superpopulation means and standard deviations, calculate the “true” model parameters and the variances of the variability terms for models F, G*, G, Q* and Q according to the theoretical outline in the “Study of hierarchical modeling in the context of a superpopulation model”.

steps.title: Generate explanatory variables
steps.instruction: Generate explanatory variable vectors by drawing from normal distributions with the corresponding means and standard deviations: X_I for model F (size nI), Z_II for model G (size nII), P_III for model Q (size nIII), and P_U for the whole population U.

steps.title: Compute analytical predictor variances
steps.instruction: Calculate the variances of the 3pHMB and 3pHHY predictors using equations (8a) and (11) based on the results from the true model parameters (Step 2) and the generated explanatory variables (Step 3).

steps.title: Monte Carlo simulation
steps.instruction: Repeat the following four sub‑steps one million (1,000,000) times:

substeps.instruction: 5a: Randomly generate variability terms for models F, G*, G, Q* and Q using the true variances from Step 2; then generate the corresponding response variables for every element in each dataset.
5b: Estimate the model parameters from the simulated data; predict the AOI population mean using 3pHMB inference; record the predicted value for this iteration.
5c: Draw a simple random sample without replacement from P_U; predict the AOI population mean using 3pHHY inference; record the predicted value for this iteration.
5d: Apply the variance estimators to the simulated outcomes to estimate the variance of the 3pHMB and 3pHHY predictors; record these variance estimates for the iteration.

steps.title: Summarize Monte Carlo results
steps.instruction: After completing all 1,000,000 iterations, compute the empirical variances of the recorded 3pHMB and 3pHHY predictions, calculate the average of the estimated variances across iterations, and compare these empirical values with the analytical variances obtained in Step 4.
